cards.heading: Console
cards.body: The console port gives out-of-band access with a rollover/USB cable, even when the network is down. It's the first way into a new device.

cards.heading: Telnet and SSH
cards.body: Remote CLI access goes through the VTY lines. Telnet (TCP 23) sends everything, including passwords, in clear text. SSH (TCP 22) encrypts the session; always use SSH and restrict the VTY lines to it. 'transport input ssh' controls which protocols may connect in ('transport output' controls sessions started from the device). 'line vty 0 15' configures 16 lines, since the range includes both ends; older devices had only vty 0 4 (5 lines).
cards.example:
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh

cards.heading: HTTP and HTTPS
cards.body: Many devices, especially WLCs, offer a web GUI. HTTP (TCP 80) is clear text; HTTPS (TCP 443) is encrypted. Disable plain HTTP: 'no ip http server', 'ip http secure-server'. 'ip http secure-server' turns on the HTTPS web interface.

cards.heading: Centralised authentication
cards.body: Instead of local accounts on every device, AAA servers check logins centrally. TACACS+ (Cisco, TCP 49) encrypts the whole payload and separates authorisation, so it suits device administration. RADIUS (UDP 1812/1813) suits network access such as Wi-Fi and 802.1X. RADIUS encrypts only the password; TACACS+ encrypts the whole body. With 200 devices, central AAA means one place to add or remove admins, and TACACS+ can authorise individual commands and log what each admin ran. Keep a local account as a fallback.

cards.heading: In-band, out-of-band and cloud
cards.body: In-band management uses the production network (SSH to an SVI). Out-of-band uses a separate path such as the console or a dedicated management port and network, so it works during outages. Cloud-managed devices are configured from a vendor dashboard.

cards.heading: Managing a layer 2 switch
cards.body: A layer 2 switch has no routed ports, so it gets its management address on an SVI in the management VLAN. To be reachable from other subnets it also needs 'ip default-gateway', because it doesn't route.
cards.example:
interface vlan 99
 ip address 10.99.0.11 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
ip default-gateway 10.99.0.1

cards.heading: Hardening the VTY lines
cards.body: 'exec-timeout 5 0' logs out a session after 5 minutes and 0 seconds idle ('0 0' disables the timeout, which isn't recommended). To let only admin hosts connect, permit them in a standard ACL and apply it to the lines with 'access-class': on lines it's access-class, on interfaces it's ip access-group. That protects remote access whichever interface it arrives on.
cards.example:
access-list 10 permit 10.99.0.0 0.0.0.255
line vty 0 15
 exec-timeout 5 0
 access-class 10 in
 transport input ssh
